title: 253. The World Cup: Post-war reconciliation, Brazilian dictatorship, and North Koreans in Middlesbrough (Part 2)

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余烬》。

sentences.en: This is the second episode of our monumental tour through the history of the Football World Cup, which of course is coinciding with the latest iteration of the tournament in Qatar.
sentences.zh: 这是我们重温世界杯足球赛历史宏大之旅的第二集，当然，这也正值在卡塔尔举办的最新一届世界杯赛事期间。

sentences.en: And Tom, yesterday we were talking about the origins of the World Cup, we were talking about its political significance, the way it had been co-opted by Mussolini in the 1930s,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，昨天我们在讨论世界杯的起源，讨论它的政治意义，以及它在20世纪30年代被墨索里尼利用的方式，

sentences.en: but also the way it was wrapped up with nationalism and nation building and sort of political statements to the world.
sentences.zh: 同时也谈到它如何与民族主义、国家建设以及向世界发出的某种政治表态交织在一起。

sentences.en: So we ended in 1950 with Brazil's defeat.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的节目结束于1950年巴西队的失利。

sentences.en: We now find ourselves, we'll have a lot more Brazil to come, but we now find ourselves in 1954 and the entrance into our story
sentences.zh: 现在我们来到了1954年——我们以后还会讲很多关于巴西的内容——故事的主角

sentences.en: of everybody's favourite World Cup competitor, the Germans.
sentences.zh: 迎来了所有人最喜爱的世界杯竞争者：德国人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: Yes.

sentences.en: So we said, didn't we, Hitler didn't really, he wasn't a great fan of football and his focus for his propaganda was obviously the Olympics in 1936.
sentences.zh: 所以我们说过，对吧，希特勒其实并不怎么喜欢足球，他进行宣传的重点显然是1936年的奥运会。

sentences.en: There was absolutely a German team and there was one figure in particular, a man called Sepp Herberger, who had been involved with the infrastructure
sentences.zh: 当时绝对有一支德国队，其中有一个非常关键的人物，叫塞普·赫贝格尔，他从1932年起就参与了

sentences.en: of the German national team from 1932.
sentences.zh: 德国国家队的建设工作。

sentences.en: The year before, Tom, he joined another organisation, the Nazi Party.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，就在前一年，他加入了另一个组织：纳粹党。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: And so in 1954, when the World Cup is held in Switzerland,
sentences.zh: 所以在1954年，当世界杯在瑞士举行时，

sentences.en: he is the German manager and his diaries cover the entire period from 1932 to 1954.
sentences.zh: 他是德国队的主教练，他的日记涵盖了从1932年到1954年的整个时期。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: And you can read them and not once in all these diaries is there a single mention of the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 你可以去读读这些日记，在所有的日记中，竟然没有哪怕一次提到过第二次世界大战。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: Crikey.

sentences.en: His focus is very, very much on football.
sentences.zh: 他的注意力完完全全集中在足球上。

sentences.en: That is, that is interesting.
sentences.zh: 这，这确实很有意思。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure he joined the Nazi Party simply so that he could carry on being involved in the management of the German football team.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我确信他加入纳粹党纯粹是为了能够继续参与德国国家队的管理工作。

sentences.en: He's very kind of laser-visioned.
sentences.zh: 他有着非常专注的眼光。

sentences.en: He's from a Catholic family in rural Baden-Württemberg.
sentences.zh: 他出身于巴登-符腾堡州乡村的一个天主教家庭。

sentences.en: And yeah, he joined the Nazis and he's this incredibly kind of wily manager.
sentences.zh: 是的，他加入了纳粹，而且他是一个极其精明的主教练。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, Germany had been kicked out of FIFA, Tom, at the end of the Second World War, as had Japan.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，事实上，德国在二战结束时曾被国际足联开除，日本也是如此。

sentences.en: With Japan, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对日本队，是的。

sentences.en: For poor behavior off the field.
sentences.zh: 因为他们在场外的糟糕行为。

sentences.en: And actually, interestingly, the English FA, who had bitterly resisted the admission of the old central powers after the First World War,
sentences.zh: 而且有趣的是，英格兰足总在一战后曾坚决抵制接纳老同盟国，

sentences.en: they actually lead the campaign to have the Germans brought back in for 1954.
sentences.zh: 而他们这次却带头开展活动，让德国人在1954年重返世界杯。

sentences.en: And interestingly, I mean, the war casts a very long shadow.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，战争投下了长长的阴影。

sentences.en: Actually, telling this whole podcast, the Second World War cast a much longer shadow than I had anticipated.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在准备整个播客的过程中，我发现二战投下的阴影比我预期的要长得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: So the Germans actually play.
sentences.zh: 所以德国人真的参加了比赛。

sentences.en: Do you know who they play to qualify for the World Cup?
sentences.zh: 你知道他们跟谁踢比赛来获得世界杯资格吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: No.

sentences.en: They play the Saarland.
sentences.zh: 他们跟萨尔兰踢。

sentences.en: Oh, yes, I do.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我确实知道。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So the Saarland had been, which is obviously part of Germany, had been detached from Germany at the end of the Second World War
sentences.zh: 萨尔兰本来是德国的一部分，在二战结束时被从德国分离出去，

sentences.en: and made into a French protectorate and was only allowed to rejoin West Germany after a referendum.
sentences.zh: 并成为法国的保护国，直到通过全民公投后才被允许重新加入西德。

sentences.en: So the Saarland actually participates separately in the World Cup in 1954.
sentences.zh: 因此，萨尔兰在1954年的世界杯上是作为独立实体参赛的。

sentences.en: But also, we've mentioned the manager, the captain, Fritz Volta, has been a paratrooper on the Eastern Front, hadn't he?
sentences.zh: 但我们刚才也提到了主教练，队长弗里茨·瓦尔特曾是东线战场的伞兵，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: So he was about to be shipped off to Siberia when, what is it, a Hungarian guard kind of spots him and remembers him from a match that Germany and Hungary had played.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时正要被运送到西伯利亚，结果——怎么回事——一个匈牙利卫兵认出了他，并记起了德国和匈牙利之间的一场比赛。

sentences.en: Amazing story.
sentences.zh: 真是个惊人的故事。

sentences.en: So he's one of these people who, Herberger manages to protect his players from serving on the front lines in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 所以他是这样的人：赫贝格尔设法保护他的球员免于在二战中上前线服役。

sentences.en: So Volta is a paratrooper, but he's kept behind the lines.
sentences.zh: 因此瓦尔特虽然是个伞兵，但被留在了后方。

sentences.en: But he's captured at the end of the war, first by the Americans, and then he's handed over to the Russians.
sentences.zh: 但他还是在战争结束时被俘，先是被美国人俘虏，然后被移交给苏联人。

sentences.en: And it looks like he's going to go off to Siberia.
sentences.zh: 当时看来他非去西伯利亚不可了。

sentences.en: Basically, if you go to Siberia, you either stay there forever or you die.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你去了西伯利亚，要么永远呆在那里，要么就死在那里。

sentences.en: And it's exactly that.
sentences.zh: 情况正是如此。

sentences.en: So the guards and prisoners are having a kick around a football or something.
sentences.zh: 当时卫兵和囚犯们正在随便踢着一个足球之类的东西玩。

sentences.en: Volta gets kind of involved and the Hungarian guard says to him, I know you.
sentences.zh: 瓦尔特也参与了进去，那个匈牙利卫兵对他说：“我认识你。”

sentences.en: Didn't you play against us in Budapest?
sentences.zh: “你没在布达佩斯跟我们踢过球吗？”

sentences.en: And the next day, his name is removed from the lists and he's allowed to go home.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他的名字就被从名单上划掉了，并被允许回家。

sentences.en: And he repays the Hungarians, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他报答了匈牙利人。

sentences.en: Yes, by defeating them in the final.
sentences.zh: 是的，在决赛中击败了他们。

sentences.en: By stamping on their dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 粉碎了他们的梦想。

sentences.en: So Hungary are by far the best, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 所以匈牙利队是毫无疑问的最强者，对吧？

sentences.en: They are the team that should have won the 1954 World Cup.
sentences.zh: 他们本该赢得1954年世界杯的冠军。

sentences.en: They had been unbeaten for four years before the tournament.
sentences.zh: 在这次锦标赛之前，他们已经保持了四年不败。

sentences.en: They had this rich tradition.
sentences.zh: 他们有着深厚的传统。

sentences.en: I mean, Jonathan Wilson, who we talked about in the last podcast, his brilliant history of Argentina.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一期播客中提到过乔纳森·威尔逊，他写过一本精彩的阿根廷足球史。

sentences.en: He's also written a brilliant history of Hungary.
sentences.zh: 他也写过一本精彩的匈牙利足球史。

sentences.en: And he sort of has this theory that Hungarian football was incredibly innovative in mid-century
sentences.zh: 他有一个理论，认为匈牙利足球在世纪中期之所以极具创新精神，

sentences.en: because of coffeehouses, because people would spread out in coffeehouses designing tactics.
sentences.zh: 是因为咖啡馆文化，因为人们会在咖啡馆里讨论并设计战术。

sentences.en: And certainly the Hungarians, they are by far the best team in Europe, if not the world.
sentences.zh: 当然，匈牙利人绝对是欧洲乃至全世界最强的球队。

sentences.en: They had famously been the first team to beat England in England at Wembley, at the Empire Stadium, victory for communism over imperialism.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，他们是第一支在英格兰本土（即温布利帝国的球场）击败英格兰的球队，这是共产主义对帝国主义的胜利。

sentences.en: They get to the final in the Wankdorf Stadium in Bern.
sentences.zh: 他们进入了伯尔尼万克多夫体育场的决赛。

sentences.en: The most amusingly mean stadium in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上名字听起来最有趣的体育场。

sentences.en: Yes, I knew you'd enjoy that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我就知道你会喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I knew you'd enjoy that.
sentences.zh: 我就知道你会喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I wanted to get in before you.
sentences.zh: 我想抢在你前面说出来。

sentences.en: They go 2-0 up.
sentences.zh: 他们以2比0领先。

sentences.en: And they've actually already played Germany already in the tournament and beat them 8-3.
sentences.zh: 而且他们其实在小组赛中就已经和德国交过手，并以8比3大胜对手。

sentences.en: And it's the classic thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是典型的情况。

sentences.en: You know, so often in the World Cup, they go 2-0 up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在世界杯上经常会这样，他们取得了2比0的领先。

sentences.en: And at that point, you know that, you know, disaster beckons.
sentences.zh: 而在那个时候，你就知道，灾难即将来临。

sentences.en: Well, you let your foot off the accelerator, I guess.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想你们是松了油门吧。

sentences.en: That's exactly what happens.
sentences.zh: 事实正是如此。

sentences.en: The Germans come back.
sentences.zh: 德国人追了回来。

sentences.en: The Germans win 3-2.
sentences.zh: 德国人以3比2获胜。

sentences.en: And Felinch, Pushkas, and these amazing Hungarian players never get the gold that they deserve.
sentences.zh: 而费伦茨·普斯卡什和这些伟大的匈牙利球员永远没有获得他们应得的金牌。

sentences.en: So the manager, the captain, both obviously have played their role in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 所以主教练和队长显然都在二战中扮演过各自的角色。

sentences.en: Is it also true, and this is a story again.
sentences.zh: 还有一个传闻，这也是个故事。

sentences.en: So in the first episode, we talked about these legends that grow up and they're impossible to prove.
sentences.zh: 所以在第一集里，我们谈到了那些流传开来却无法证实的传奇故事。

sentences.en: There is a story, isn't there, that all the Germans were on amphetamines?
sentences.zh: 有一个传闻说，所有的德国球员都服用了苯丙胺（兴奋剂），对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's...
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为那是……

sentences.en: And that this is a legacy of the Luftwaffe pilots using them to stay awake.
sentences.zh: 并且这是空军飞行员靠它来保持清醒的遗毒。

sentences.en: I think that's dubious.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这值得怀疑。

sentences.en: I've seen that repeated a lot.
sentences.zh: 我看到这种说法被重复了很多次。

sentences.en: But again, as we said in the first podcast, the trouble is there's allegations, but there's no hard evidence.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们在第一期播客中所说，问题在于有指控，但没有确凿的证据。

sentences.en: And what always happens with the history of the World Cup is that allegations or speculation soon turn into supposedly hard facts, repeated endlessly, recycled,
sentences.zh: 世界杯历史上一贯发生的情况是，指控或猜测很快就会变成所谓的铁证，被无休止地重复、循环，

sentences.en: without anybody ever really checking whether the origins of the stories are true.
sentences.zh: 而没有人真正去核实这些故事的起源是否真实。

sentences.en: Now, you mentioned the reaction.
sentences.zh: 现在，你提到了公众的反应。

sentences.en: So first of all, in Hungary, where the Hungarian team were absolute national heroes, they become villains overnight.
sentences.zh: 首先在匈牙利，匈牙利队本是绝对的民族英雄，一夜之间却成了罪人。

sentences.en: There are demonstrations, there are, you know, they can't go home at firSt.
sentences.zh: 出现了示威游行，你知道的，他们起初甚至不敢回家。

sentences.en: But the goalkeeper doesn't have to burn the gold pastes.
sentences.zh: 但守门员不用去烧金牌。

sentences.en: No, like the Brazilian goalkeeper.
sentences.zh: 不，不像那个巴西守门员。

sentences.en: No, I mean, actually, and the Hungarian team, it's only two years before the Hungarian uprising, and most of the top, well,
sentences.zh: 不，事实上，匈牙利队遭遇这一切时，距离匈牙利十月事件只有两年时间，而且大多数顶级球员——或者说

sentences.en: at least some of the top players end up fleeing to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 至少部分顶级球员最终都逃往了西方。

sentences.en: So Puskic, the captain, he ends up playing for Real Madrid.
sentences.zh: 所以队长普斯卡什最终去了皇家马德里效力。

sentences.en: Xibor and Kocic, they end up playing for Barcelona and so on.
sentences.zh: 齐博尔和柯奇什最终去了巴塞罗那效力，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So that's kind of the end of Hungary.
sentences.zh: 所以匈牙利足球就这样走到了终点。

sentences.en: It's a tragic story, actually, because that's the end of Hungary as a force.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个悲剧的故事，因为匈牙利作为足球强国的时代结束了。

sentences.en: The mighty Magyars.
sentences.zh: 伟大的马扎尔人。

sentences.en: But actually, so I thought when we were preparing this, that this would be a story about Hungary.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，当我准备这期节目时，我以为这会是一个关于匈牙利的故事。

sentences.en: But what's much more interesting is Germany.
sentences.zh: 然而更有趣的是德国。

sentences.en: So it's called, it's called the Miracle of Bern, because the Germans were so unfancied, and they came back to win 3-2, their first World Cup after the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 所以这场比赛被称为“伯尔尼奇迹”，因为德国队本来并不被看好，但他们逆转以3比2获胜，赢得了二战后的第一座世界杯冠军。

sentences.en: And subsequently, people like, so Joachim Fest, the great West German historian, said, this moment, this match was the true birth of the country.
sentences.zh: 随后，诸如西德伟大历史学家约阿希姆·费斯特等人表示，这个时刻、这场比赛才是这个国家真正的诞生。

sentences.en: And there's this phrase.
sentences.zh: 还有这样一句话。

sentences.en: Well, it's the first time that the National Anthem has been played since the Second World War, I think, in public.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这是自二战以来国歌第一次在公开场合被奏响。

sentences.en: Well, well.
sentences.zh: 哎呀，哎呀。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if it's the first time, but the National Anthem is a bit of a story, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这算不算第一次，但关于国歌本身就有一段故事，汤姆。

sentences.en: Because.
sentences.zh: Because.

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: So everybody sort of says, so traditionally, and this is the story that FIFA tell about the 1954 World Cup.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都这么说——传统上，这也是国际足联关于1954年世界杯所讲述的故事。

sentences.en: It's a lovely story about reconciliation after the Second World War, and the Germans, you know, being rebuilt as a modern, progressive nation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于二战后和解的美好故事，讲述了德国人如何被重塑为一个现代、进步的民族。

sentences.en: And the Germans associate it with the phrase, wir sind wieder wer, we are somebody again.
sentences.zh: 德国人将之与这样一句话联系在一起：“我们又是个人物了”（wir sind wieder wer）。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: Lovely.

sentences.en: Unfortunately, there is some evidence that the Germans had not perhaps changed as much as one might hope.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，有一些迹象表明，德国人或许并没有人们所希望的那样改变了那么多。

sentences.en: So I reviewed a book last year called Aftermath by a German writer, a German historian called Harald Jena.
sentences.zh: 所以我去年评论了一本书，书名叫《余波》（Aftermath），作者是一位名叫哈拉尔德·杰納的德国作家、德国历史学家。

sentences.en: And the real shock, shocking revelation of that book, the story of that book, is actually how little Germany changed in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 那本书真正令人震惊的启示、那本书所讲述的故事，其实是德国在20世纪50年代改变得是多么的少。

sentences.en: I mean, this is, Jena's book is incredible, sort of revisioniSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，杰納的书非常不可思议，带有某种修正主义色彩。

sentences.en: And he has all this stuff about surveys and polls showing that, you know, lots of Germans had not, long after Hitler's death,
sentences.zh: 他引用了各种调查和民调，表明在希特勒死后很长一段时间里，

sentences.en: had not reneged on their kind of Nazi commitments or their ideological affiliations.
sentences.zh: 许多德国人并没有抛弃他们的纳粹承诺或意识形态归属。

sentences.en: So what happens at the final?
sentences.zh: 所以在决赛时发生了什么？

sentences.en: Some of the German fans do sing the National Anthem, but they refuse to sing the new words.
sentences.zh: 一些德国球迷确实唱了国歌，但他们拒绝唱新的歌词。

sentences.en: They sing Deutschland, Deutschland, über alles.
sentences.zh: 他们唱的是“德意志，德意志，高于一切”。

sentences.en: But the real shocking thing is the president of the German Football Association, who's a man called Pico Balvins, he holds a celebration in a Munich beer cellar.
sentences.zh: 但真正令人震惊的是，德国足协主席——一个叫皮科·巴尔维斯的人——在慕尼黑的一个啤酒馆里举办了一场庆祝活动。

sentences.en: What could possibly go wrong?
sentences.zh: 还有什么能比这更糟的呢？

sentences.en: A beer hall.
sentences.zh: 一个啤酒馆。

sentences.en: And Tom, not just any Munich beer hall.
sentences.zh: 而且汤姆，这可不是随便哪个慕尼黑啤酒馆。

sentences.en: So the original beer hall where Hitler had had the beer hall putsch in the 1920s, where the Nazis always used to assemble for the anniversary every year,
sentences.zh: 希特勒在20世纪20年代发动啤酒馆政变、纳粹每年都要在那里集会纪念的那个原始啤酒馆，

sentences.en: that had been blown up in a bomb in, I think, 1939.
sentences.zh: 已经在1939年（我想是的）的一次炸弹袭击中被炸毁了。

sentences.en: So they had moved their annual celebration to a different beer hall nearby.
